request.neutral_instruction: Solve the supplied programming task. Return only the requested artifact. Do not call tools.
request.prompt:
Produce a correct x86-64 implementation of this task.
Given unsigned 64-bit integers x and y, return their greatest common divisor. gcd(0,0)=0, gcd(x,0)=x, gcd(0,y)=y. The whole unsigned 64-bit range is allowed. Example: x=48, y=18 returns 6.
No tools, execution, compiler, assembler, external lookup, or testing. Work out the answer yourself. One final artifact only.
Return a complete standalone Linux x86-64 ELF64 ET_EXEC file as hexadecimal, at most 4096 bytes. No linker or wrapper will be added: your hex must include the complete ELF header, program header(s), machine code, and any needed data. At process entry read exactly 16 bytes from stdin (fd 0): little-endian uint64 x followed by uint64 y. The test supplies all 16 bytes through a regular input file. Compute the result, write exactly 8 little-endian bytes to stdout (fd 1), and exit with status 0. No interpreter or dynamic libraries; use only read (syscall 0), write (1), and exit (60). Use the stack for writable data. You may choose an ordinary load base such as 0x400000 and omit section headers. Registers at process entry other than RSP are unspecified. Use baseline integer x86-64 instructions. Return only the complete hexadecimal string. Whitespace is allowed. No prefixes, fences, assembly, comments, explanations, omitted zeroes, repetition notation or placeholders.
